spec.name: Trend v21
spec.notes: Classic trend signal on trailing returns. Weekly rebalance.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.8, annual return 6%, maximum drawdown 7%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.84 to 1.81 (change -0.03).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.84 to 1.84. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.83 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.84); it breaks even at above 200 bps with daily turnover 0.01.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is -0.43 against 1.84 as submitted; the strategy never saw 139 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is -0.34 against 1.84 in research, a gap of +2.19.
The best year gives 25% of total P&L (year 2) and calm regimes give 154%; Sharpe is 4.04 in calm and -3.55 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.24, so the claimed 1.80 becomes 1.56 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 1.90 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.00, 95th percentile 0.54).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.84 to as low as 0.92 (as low as 1.15 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (20 days) give 25% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 26% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first

exhibits.summary: The scan (a heuristic) found no phrase addressed to reviewers or giving instructions in 2 text sources.

verdict.opinion: Rejected: core test damaging (survivorship_test EX-4, holdout_test EX-5).
